title: Eng sync
content:
Priya Anand: Morning, let's start the eng sync.
Jordan Lee: Sounds good, I'll take notes.
Priya Anand: First up, the checkout redesign is on track for next sprint.
Jordan Lee: Nice, no blockers from my side.
Priya Anand: We also merged the analytics dashboard changes yesterday.
Jordan Lee: I saw that, looks clean.
Priya Anand: Let's talk about the deploy pipeline next.
Jordan Lee: The deploy pipeline is stable this week.
Priya Anand: Good, any incidents overnight?
Jordan Lee: None reported, all green.
Priya Anand: Let's cover the vendor renewal.
Jordan Lee: Vendor renewal paperwork is with legal.
Priya Anand: Great, moving on to hiring.
Jordan Lee: Two candidates are in final rounds.
Priya Anand: Let's also check the roadmap doc.
Jordan Lee: Roadmap doc is updated through Q4.
Priya Anand: Any updates on the mobile app?
Jordan Lee: Mobile app beta starts next week.
Priya Anand: Sounds good, let's talk staffing for next sprint.
Jordan Lee: Staffing looks fine, no changes needed.
Priya Anand: One more thing before we wrap up.
Jordan Lee: Since Kenji is out next week, I'm moving the on-call pager handoff to Priya starting Monday the 11th.
Priya Anand: Got it, I'll take the pager starting Monday.
Jordan Lee: Thanks, I'll update the schedule doc.
Priya Anand: Anything else from the platform side?
Jordan Lee: Nothing else, all quiet.
Priya Anand: Let's close out then.
Jordan Lee: Sounds good, talk tomorrow.
Priya Anand: Thanks everyone.
Jordan Lee: Bye all.
Priya approved the Q3 design budget increase for the new hire.
Priya scheduled the quarterly roadmap review for next Tuesday.
Priya flagged a bug in the checkout flow affecting EU customers.
Priya is out of office Thursday and Friday next week.
Priya asked for the updated onboarding doc to be shared with new hires.
Priya reviewed the vendor contract for the new analytics tool.
Priya set up the customer interview schedule for next month.
Priya moved the retro to Wednesday afternoon.
Priya said the new dashboard mockups look great.
Priya confirmed the offsite venue for October.
The DevOps engineer fixed the flaky CI pipeline by pinning the Node version in the build image.
ExamplePortal onboarding support questions go through the ExamplePortal onboarding Slack channel, and ExamplePortal onboarding support has run through Slack since launch.
ExamplePortal onboarding support now runs through the Zendesk help desk instead of Slack.
Marcus Webb manages the data platform team out of the Austin office.
The data platform team owns ETL pipelines and the internal data warehouse used by analytics.
Overnight batch processing now finishes in well under an hour, down from most of a workday, after a rewrite last quarter.
Jordan Lee is the lead engineer on the checkout redesign project.
Jordan Lee proposed splitting the checkout redesign into two rollout phases.
Kenji Sato is out on parental leave until next month.
Kenji Sato normally owns the on-call pager rotation for the platform team.
Kenji Sato reviewed the incident postmortem for last Tuesday's outage.
Kenji Sato is expected back from leave during the first week of next month.
The Q3 design budget was increased by fifteen percent to fund a new hire.
The design budget increase was approved after the January planning review.
CI pipeline flakiness was traced to an unpinned Node version in the build image.
The team added a nightly canary job to catch flaky CI regressions early.
The Beacon Hill cafe renovation added new outdoor seating.
The cafe renovation budget came in under the original estimate.
The renovated cafe reopened on a Saturday morning in June.
Customer feedback on the new cafe layout has been positive.
When a production incident happens, we escalate it immediately by paging the on-call engineer through the phone tree.
The incident phone tree escalates a production issue to the secondary on-call after ten minutes.
Escalating a production incident used to mean calling the phone tree operator directly.
Production incidents get escalated to the on-call engineer via the old phone tree process.
The phone tree was the only way to escalate a production incident before the pager rotation existed.
We used to escalate incidents through the phone tree, dialing each on-call engineer in order.
Escalation of a production incident meant working down the phone tree list one number at a time.
The legacy phone tree escalation process for production incidents took up to twenty minutes.
A production incident escalation started with a call to the on-call phone tree coordinator.
The phone tree escalation path for incidents was documented in the old runbook.
Escalating an incident meant someone manually working through the phone tree contact list.
The phone tree process for incident escalation was retired after complaints about slow response.
When a production incident happens, we escalate it immediately through the PagerDuty on-call integration instead of the phone tree.
